title: Nvidia’s Vera CPU Enters the Server Market as Company Pushes Beyond GPUs Into AI Infrastructure
excerpt: The 88-core Arm-based processor outperforms Intel Xeon chips in early benchmarks and trades blows with AMD’s top EPYC models, as Nvidia targets the agentic AI workload market.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Nvidia's Vera CPU features 88 Arm v9.2 cores and delivers 1.2 TB/s memory bandwidth.
  • In benchmarks, Vera outperformed Intel Xeon by 1.5x and AMD EPYC by 10%.
  • Japan's Noetra consortium ordered 13,750 Vera CPUs for a national AI factory starting in 2027.
  • Nvidia anticipates $1 trillion in revenue from AI infrastructure between 2025 and 2027.

Nvidia is no longer content to dominate the AI market through GPUs alone. The company’s Vera CPU, unveiled at GTC 2026 in March, is now heading to customers as Nvidia’s most serious bid to challenge AMD and Intel in the server processor market.

Michael Larabel of Phoronix, who tested the chip at Nvidia’s Santa Clara headquarters, called it the “most performant ARM Linux server processor” he has tested in the outlet’s 22-year history, according to TechSpot.

Architecture and Performance

Vera is built around 88 custom Arm v9.2 “Olympus” cores with a feature called Spatial Multithreading, which physically partitions core resources rather than time-slicing them. The result is 176 threads from a single monolithic compute die — no chiplet design, no NUMA eccentricities, and uniform latency to every core.

https://x.com/nvidia/status/2079240931337965928

The memory subsystem sets Vera apart from x86 competitors. Nvidia specifies up to 1.2 TB/s of total bandwidth via LPDDR5X SOCAMM modules, roughly 14 GB/s per core — about three times the per-core bandwidth of traditional data center CPUs, according to Nvidia.

“The difference from Grace to Vera was consistently exceeding my expectations for gen-on-gen performance we typically see for processors.”

— Michael Larabel, Phoronix

In benchmarks, Vera compiled a default Linux kernel in 20 seconds — the fastest result Phoronix has ever recorded. It delivered a 1.5x overall performance advantage over Intel’s latest 128-core Xeon Granite Rapids processor and beat AMD’s EPYC 9575F by 10% on a geometric mean basis.

The Agentic AI Angle

Unlike traditional server CPUs designed for general-purpose workloads, Vera is purpose-built for what Nvidia calls “agentic AI” — systems that plan, reason, and execute tasks autonomously across multiple steps. These workloads demand massive CPU compute alongside GPU acceleration.

> **"Three direct customers accounted for 54% of total sales, highlighting the concentration risk."** https://youtube.com/watch?v=8cO9OTjk5H0

“When we think Vera Rubin, we think the entire system, vertically integrated, complete with software, extended end to end, optimized as one giant system,” CEO Jensen Huang said at GTC 2026.

Vera integrates native FP8 operations directly on the CPU cores and supports a 6x128-bit SVE2 vector implementation, allowing certain AI workloads to execute without relying on external accelerators.

Major Deals Already Signed

The processor’s commercial momentum is building. Japan’s Noetra consortium — led by SoftBank, Sony, Honda, and NEC — has ordered 13,750 Vera CPUs alongside 27,500 Rubin GPUs for a national AI factory delivering 140 megawatts of data center capacity. Construction is expected to begin in April 2027.

Meta has signed a deal to deploy millions of Nvidia chips, including standalone CPUs and Vera Rubin rack systems, according to CNBC. Bristol Myers Squibb became the first life sciences company to purchase a Vera Rubin-based DGX SuperPOD for drug discovery research.

Competition Ahead

Vera faces a tightening competitive field. AMD’s next-generation EPYC Venice, based on the Zen 6 architecture, is already in mass production and slated for the second half of 2026. Intel is preparing its Diamond Rapids platform. Qualcomm and Arm are developing their own data-center-specific CPUs.

Crucially, Phoronix was unable to test power consumption during its benchmarks because Nvidia is still optimizing Vera’s power management. For Arm-based processors, efficiency is a key selling point — and that data remains missing.

![Intel Xeon. In benchmarks, Vera outperformed Intel Xeon by 1.5x and AMD EPYC by 10%.](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/3/31/Intel-Xeon-Badge-2024.jpg)

What to Watch

Nvidia generated $75.2 billion in data center revenue last quarter, up 92% year over year. Three direct customers accounted for 54% of total sales, highlighting the concentration risk. Vera’s push into sovereign AI projects and enterprise deployments could help diversify that customer base as the company targets what it calls a $1 trillion revenue opportunity through 2027.
